tts: Knitting seems to be having a moment. That lamp post that you never noticed before is suddenly multicoloured. Trees, statues, even buses and bridges are finding themselves decorated with a warm, brightly coloured knitted woollen cover. It is called yarn-bombing.

It is believed to have started in the United States, but it is now a global phenomenon. In Paris a yarn-bomber has filled the cracks in the pavement with brightly knitted wool. In Poland, the well-known yarn-bomber Agata Oleksiak has covered her grandmother’s country house with a loose knitted cover. And in Mexico City, the artist Magda Sayeg has specially designed a perfectly fitting cover for a city bus.

It is a kind of street art, a little like graffiti, but considerably less damaging, as it can easily be removed. Nonetheless, many local governments do not like yarn-bombing, and therefore it is often done secretly at night. Yarn-bombing is very quiet.

items.q: What is yarn-bombing?
o: Covering street objects in knitted wool
A kind of graffiti sprayed at night

items.q: Why is it usually done at night?
o: Many local governments do not like it
It is easier to knit in the dark

items.q: How does the speaker compare it with graffiti?
o: It is far less damaging, because it can be removed

tts: It is very much a social thing, with groups of knitters working together to plan and create something. Even the well-known yarn-bombing artists, such as Oleksiak and Sayeg, have teams of people to assist them with the bigger projects.
The yarn-bombers then take photos of their creations and post them online for others to admire.

So why do they do it? Unlike much graffiti, yarn-bombing is often very much about making an ugly public space or object more beautiful. It is about putting something personal and handmade into an urban, industrial environment. And of course it aims to put a smile on people’s faces.

items.s: Well-known artists have teams to help with bigger projects.
The results are photographed and posted online.
The aim, unlike much graffiti, is to make an ugly object more beautiful.
The speaker says the point is to shock people.

tts: My partner always has music on while she works, whereas I prefer silence. Is this just a personal preference, or is one actually better than the other?

According to Professor Ravi Mehta, a moderate level of noise is better for our creativity than silence. So quiet music is a good idea. Too much noise is not good, though — especially listening to other people’s telephone conversations. This is particularly distracting because our brain is automatically trying to solve the puzzle of what is being said by the person we cannot hear.
One study from Cornell University showed that when temperatures were lower, at twenty degrees Celsius, employees made forty-four per cent more mistakes than when it was twenty-five.
Ever been told “tidy desk, tidy mind”? Apparently, having a messy desk is actually better for being inventive.
When we are tired, our brain is less efficient, but it is also more likely to make new connections.

acts.title: The pairs that catch everybody
rule: These are not synonyms and they are not spelling variants. Each pair contains two different words that happen to look or sound similar, and every one of them appears in B2 exam scripts as an error. The only reliable method is to learn the pair together, with a sentence for each.
points: lose is a verb: to stop having. loose is an adjective: not tight. Different vowels, different words.
advise is the verb, with an s. advice is the noun, with a c. Advice is uncountable: a piece of advice.
affect is almost always the verb, effect almost always the noun. It affects me; it has an effect on me.
especially = above all, more than others. specially = for one particular purpose.
quite is an adverb of degree; quiet is an adjective meaning without noise. Only the spelling is close.
In British English, practice is the noun and practise the verb. American English uses practice for both.
eg: We had nothing to lose and everything to gain.
The covers are quite loose, so they are easy to fit.
I would advise you not to do it during the day.
Shall I give you some advice?
Too much noise can affect your concentration.
The effect of the knitting is quite striking.
Too much noise is bad, especially half a phone call.
She specially designed a cover for that bus.
The office is quite noisy in the afternoon.
acts.careful: “Can you give me an advice?” is the single most frequent error in this set. advice is uncountable: some advice, a piece of advice, two pieces of advice.

write.q: Write about 180 words giving your view on street art in your city — where it works, where it does not, and what you would advise the council to do. Use at least four of the confusable pairs from this lesson, and use both halves of at least two of those pairs.
write.model:
In our city there is almost no street art in the centre and a great deal of it on the walls behind the old bus depot, which is quite the wrong way round.

What works is the depot. Nobody had to ask permission, the wall was specially prepared by whoever went first, and the effect after five years is a stretch of concrete that people photograph. It has not damaged anything, because there was nothing there to lose.

What does not work is the tagging on the apartment blocks. That is loose, hurried and unimaginative, and it affects how people feel about their own stairwell, especially the older residents.

My advice to the council would be simple and cheap. Do not remove the depot wall. Give three more walls the same status, choose them badly-lit and quiet, and see what happens. Painting over everything costs money every year and has had no effect at all.
